answer: Tie each agent seat to one living operator through a biometric uniqueness check: an orb scans the operator's iris, keeps only a zero-knowledge nullifier, and the ledger refuses any second seat derived from the same eye. A farmer can rack a thousand keys on servers out in the tundra, but he owns just two irises, so his fleet collapses to one seat. Honest agents climb that trellis of one-human-one-seat, and the registry stays a haven no sybil can flood, with no raw scan ever stored.
